doc.title: Alicia Olatuja interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 9, 2018

title: Audience question: her band and her guitarist David
summary: She explains how she chooses band members and how guitarist David proved himself at her senior recital.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: I just had a question about whether you’d made it with the same band that you started out with or how you find a talent that will match yours you know?

Well that’s a good question. He knows about that. Well I actually have band members that I play with more than others because they are just there and they are amazing. But sometimes, depending on budget or depending on just curiosity even, with special guests and things like that, I might switch up something. Or if I’m playing on the west coast versus the east coast or if I’m traveling to another country, sometimes we’re invited to do my repertoire but with the band that plays at a particular venue. I will say that my

guitarist is somebody that I had a senior recital, the guitarist I had did not learn the music, he didn’t practice, he came, he showed up, he was terrible and then he blamed it on everybody. “This isn’t my type of music.” I’m like, “You just didn’t practice.” But my recital was like coming up in three days and you know, recitals are hard. Like I was pulling in classical music and jazz and I was freaking out. And someone said, “I know this great guitarist, he’s amazing.” I think he was like a sophomore. And I was like “Whatever, just bring him in here.” And he was like okay, he took the music, he went away, he shed that music, he practiced, he showed up at the rehearsal and nailed it. And I was like, “Dude, you’re going to be my American Express I’m never leaving home without you.” Like anywhere I can go, if I can take you, I will take you. And so David, he’s here tonight too with me. But I’d rather have no guitarist than be forced to play with like a bunch of other guitarists because he can’t make it.
And that’s the way it is, too.
Yeah. I’ll be like I just won’t have one.
Yeah. And you’ll hear why. You’re all coming to the show, right? Okay.
